verdict.rationale: Box's own docs offer a free developer account that uses the same API with a developer token. Community reports confirm a free consumer tier with a 250 MB file-size cap and 10 GB monthly bandwidth, but no first-party published storage quota appears in the evidence. missing for 10: first-party published free-tier storage quota, documentation that the free tier works with the same desktop/mobile clients, current independent corroboration of free-tier limits

support.subject: As a power user, I can start free — a real free tier with published storage quota that works with the same clients and API

citations.quote: Sign up for a Box free developer account, generate the developer token and make your first API call.
Replace <ACCESS_TOKEN> with a developer token and run: curl https://api.box.com/2.0/users/me
Max file size is 250 megabyte on Box's free tier
There's only 10GB of bandwidth for the month on Box's free tier
